message.content:
Yes, Coca-Cola originally contained cocaine, though the amount was relatively small and it was removed long ago.

## The History

Coca-Cola was invented in 1886 by **Dr. John Stith Pemberton**, an Atlanta pharmacist. He originally created a drink called "Pemberton's French Wine Coca," which was inspired by a European "coca wine" called Vin Mariani. When Atlanta passed temperance laws banning alcohol in 1886, Pemberton reformulated the drink as a non-alcoholic soda fountain beverage, keeping the coca leaf extract and adding kola nut (for caffeine), sugar, and caramel coloring.

At the time, **cocaine was legal and commonly used in patent medicines**. The earliest batches of Coca-Cola reportedly contained about **9mg of cocaine per glass**. The "Coca" in Coca-Cola does refer to the coca leaf, while "Cola" comes from the kola nut.

## When It Was Removed

The cocaine content was gradually reduced and eventually eliminated:

- **1903**: The Coca-Cola Company stopped using fresh coca leaves and switched to "spent" or **de-cocainized coca leaves**, which contained only trace amounts of cocaine.
- **By 1929**: The formula was **completely cocaine-free**.

The removal was driven by shifting public attitudes toward cocaine, growing regulations, and racial prejudices of the era—cocaine became stigmatized when its recreational use spread in Black neighborhoods, though it had been acceptable among affluent white consumers.

## Today

Modern Coca-Cola still uses a **coca leaf extract**, but it is processed by the **Stepan Company** in New Jersey—the only DEA-authorized facility in the U.S. to import coca leaves. They remove all cocaine from the extract before it goes to Coca-Cola. The extracted cocaine is sold to Mallinckrodt, a pharmaceutical company, for approved medical uses.

Coca-Cola officially denies that cocaine was ever an "added ingredient," though most independent historical sources confirm there were at least trace amounts in the original formula.

2. https://www.thetakeout.com/1788713/why-coca-cola-had-cocaine/
3. https://www.avenuesrecovery.com/understanding-addiction/cocaine-and-crack-addiction/was-there-cocaine-in-coca-cola/
4. https://thetraininggyms.com/blog/coca-cola-is-worse-than-cocaine/
